record.context_brief: Fundamental group and Albanese fibers under semi-positive curvature
record.original_question: Let (X, g) be a compact Kahler manifold with semi-positive holomorphic sectional curvature. Is the fundamental group of X an extension of a finite group by Z^(2m)? After passing to a suitable finite etale cover X* -> X and considering the Albanese map alpha: X* -> Alb(X*), does the fiber F carry a Kahler metric g_F with ntf(F, g_F) = dim F, and is F projective and rationally connected?

evidence.quote: Problem 3.6 (cf. [Mat21, Problem 5.2]). Let (X, g) be a compact Kahler manifold with semi-positive holomorphic sectional curvature.
Is the fundamental group of X is an extension of a finite group by Z
Does the fiber F admit a Kahler metric gF such that ntf(F, gF ) = dim F?
Is the fiber F projective and rationally connected?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(X,g)$ be a compact Kähler manifold of complex dimension $n$ with semi-positive holomorphic sectional curvature, i.e. $H_g(v) := R_g(v,\bar v, v,\bar v) \ge 0$ for every nonzero tangent vector $v \in T_X$. For a Kähler manifold $(Y,g_Y)$, define the "number of truly flat directions" $\mathrm{ntf}(Y,g_Y)$ at a generic point $y \in Y$ to be the maximal complex dimension of a subspace $V \subset T_{Y,y}$ such that $R_{g_Y}(v,\bar w, \cdot, \cdot) = 0$ for all $v,w \in V$ (equivalently, the maximal dimension of a "truly flat" subspace of the tangent space).

Address the following questions:

(a) Is the fundamental group $\pi_1(X)$ an extension
$$1 \longrightarrow \mathbb{Z}^{2m} \longrightarrow \pi_1(X) \longrightarrow G \longrightarrow 1$$
where $G$ is a finite group and $2m = 2\dim \mathrm{Alb}(X^*)$ for some finite étale cover $X^* \to X$?

(b) Does there exist a finite étale cover $\pi: X^* \to X$ such that, denoting by $\alpha: X^* \to \mathrm{Alb}(X^*)$ the Albanese map, $\alpha$ is a surjective submersion and a general fiber $F$ admits a Kähler metric $g_F$ with $\mathrm{ntf}(F,g_F) = \dim F$?

(c) Under the conclusion of (b), is the fiber $F$ projective and rationally connected?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is the subject of active research. Significant progress has been made: for compact Kähler surfaces the structure (rationally connected, complex torus, or ruled surface over an elliptic curve) is known, and recent work (e.g., on quasi-positive mixed curvature and RC-positive metrics, including results of Matsumura and collaborators) establishes projectivity and rational connectedness of fibers under stronger hypotheses such as quasi-positive holomorphic sectional curvature or absence of truly flat tangent vectors. The full conjectural picture (parts (a)–(c) together) for general compact Kähler manifolds with merely semi-positive holomorphic sectional curvature does not appear to be completely resolved.

status_evidence.title: Compact Kähler manifolds with quasi-positive holomorphic sectional curvature (Zhang talk)
status_evidence.snippet: If the manifold has no nonzero truly flat tangent vector at some point, then it must be projective and rationally connected, answering a problem raised by Yang and Matsumura.
status_evidence.claim: A version of the problem under stronger 'no truly flat tangent vector' hypotheses has been answered, indicating partial resolution.

status_evidence.title: Quasi-positive mixed curvature, vanishing theorems, and rational connectedness
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes rational connectedness results under quasi-positive curvature conditions.
status_evidence.claim: Partial results toward the rational-connectedness portion of the conjecture exist.

status_evidence.title: On the image of MRC fibrations of projective manifolds with semi-positive holomorphic sectional curvature
status_evidence.snippet: Studies the MRC fibration and Albanese map of such manifolds, with finite covers being fiber bundles over the Albanese torus with rationally connected fibers in the projective case.
status_evidence.claim: Structural Albanese/MRC results are known in the projective setting.
